When ["Our Origins"]

"The people of this world can be grouped into
three categories: animal folk, witches, and
non-magical humans. While there is some overlap,
our human forms are our single uniting factor.
"Animal folk are born in a wide variety of forms,
believed to be their true forms, which they are
able to return to under various conditions, and
which they MUST return to at death.
"The main identifying factor of a witch is their
ability to command magic of all sorts. Though
they are capable of transforming themselves,
their natural state is humanoid.
"Non-magical humans are classified by their
lack of inherent abilities or talents relating
to magic, as the name suggests. Like witches,
they are born and die in human form.
"The most broadly accepted theory of humankind's
origin is that witches divided into each group:
one set cursed to their strange inhuman forms,
and another set who abandoned magic entirely.
"It is also plausible to say non-magical humans
are the ones who learned magic to become witches,
giving way to an obsession with transformation,
which then led to the existence of animal folk...
"...but until we find evidence favoring either of
these theories, we can only hopelessly guess.
It remains the world's greatest mystery."

When ["Other Worlds"]

"There is no current estimate toward the number
of alternate worlds in existence, though we have
been able to travel to a small handful due to
the efforts of powerful witches.
"The most notable world we have been able to
connect to is known as the Netherworld. This realm
is inhabited by creatures called demons, and
has gone largely unexplored due to its vastness.
"We have very little information on other worlds
and their histories, but it is abundantly clear
something higher than magic has bridged the gaps
between existing worlds long before us.
"Although the worlds we know have all developed
independently, there are striking, impossible to
ignore similarities between them: specifically
the common humanoid forms, and the names of gods.
"The existence of gods is surrounded by mystery.
Most of the information gathered on the subject
is unreliable, as many legends have been passed
down through unverifiable oral tradition.
"Though gods are elusive in nature, the fact that
they are known by the same names across dimensions
is proof enough for many that they truly do exist."

Believe it or not, there was a time
this old rabbit hated wolves.
Hard to imagine, eh?
I used to live in a town near here,
with my wife and 8 children.
The youngest... why, she'd be about
your age now, Trick.
One day, out foraging with my daughter...
wouldn't you know it, the first time
I bring her along on my usual route,
we cross paths with a wolf!
I told her to run home as fast as her
little legs would carry her...
then I gave that wolf the what for!
Oughta be ashamed, scaring a child.
But not long into my lecturin'...
The mountain rumbled and roared,
and we quickly realized we'd been
caught in an avalanche!
Thank my lucky stars, I survived.
My right leg was broke though,
must've banged it against a rock. But,
I was too worked up to pay it any mind.
I burrowed my way out of the snow
pretty easy. Then, when I poked my
head out, I came face to face with
that wolf! Fangs, claws, and all!
Y'see, I'd always been told that a wolf
who's ready to kill takes its beast form.
Easier to rend its prey like that.
Seeing him just about scared me to death!
"Please don't eat me!
I have a wife and 8 children!"
I begged him.
And he blinked at me in return.
"Do you want to return to them?"
I'd never expected a question like that
to come from behind those huge fangs.
I didn't know what to say.
"If you give me somethin' to eat,
I'll carry you to the main road.
You can reach your home from there,"
he said.
So I opened up my rucksack and
handed over the only food I had.
One measly rice ball.
Surely not enough to sate a wolf.
But wouldn'tcha know it,
he took it anyway.
He lifted me right up out of the snow,
and we stumbled our way back to
the main road, just as he promised.
And when it came time to part ways...
"Why didn't you eat me back there?
If you were hungry, my meat would've
done you better than a plain old
rice ball," I said to him.
"I have a daughter too," he told me.
"When I looked at you,
I thought of that."
Those words hit me hard... but,
there was one more thing bothering me.
"Why'd you change form if you were
never going to hurt me?" I asked him.
"Easier to dig someone out of the snow
with big paws like these."
It'd never occured to me.
I broke down cryin' when he said that.
I'd treated him so wrong, meanwhile
all he's done is help me out.
I felt so ashamed.
I didn't have it in me to return home,
not in that state... my heart was just
as broke as my leg!
I couldn't bear for my family to be
stuck lookin' after a fool like me.
I asked that wolf to take me back
to his home, 'til I was healed up.
But my leg's never been quite the same...
I only would've been a burden to them.
Can't work a farm when just standin's
a lot to ask of ya.
Every day that passed, it got
harder and harder to go back home...
I wasn't ever able to muster the courage.
But I've learned so much,
thanks to Cotton...
Thanks to everyone.
Even if I'm not always welcome.
Hah... it has a sad ending, but you
still always listen all the way through.
You're a kind wolf, Trick.

Let me tell you a story.

now, right? Well, long before that...
We were part of a much larger group
here on Mount Sorbet. A group that
couldn't get by on foraging alone.
Some would buy sanctioned meat from
the witches. But some... were hunters.
We avoid wolves like that now, but
they're still out there on this mountain.
I'm worried... that many people
may have the wrong idea about wolves.
I'm worried about what Treat might
have to face, leaving the pack like this.
I don't think it's wrong for them
to be afraid... wherever Treat goes,
I believe she'll be able to show them
that she means no harm.

they'll see that you're kind as well.

not giving me a farewell speech.

I shouldn't keep you.
You have an adventure to go on,
after all.

Treat all paying customers with respect.

A conspiracy that destroyed my name,
a lie that crumbled an empire.

Old wounds, at this point.

When [what is this place?]

The InsteRail uses spacial and
temporal magic in order to transport
matter anywhere in an instant!
It's primarily used for long distance
traversal, but we also offer limited
time travel services to customers
with an Anytime Pass.
Wow, time travel?
Sounds awesome... how would you
get a pass for that?
Oh, they're VERY expensive.
You also need to be licensed to use it
due to regulations against frivolous
creation of alternate universes.
Sounds like a lot of trouble...
Wouldn't be fair if it was easy,
I guess.
Haha, I hear that a lot.
In the meantime, we hope you'll
get the most out of our spatial
travel services.

When [how does it work?]

The InsteRail is a railway system
with stations all over the world,
even spanning across dimensions!
As long as the rails between stations
are connected, you'll be able to
access them via this chamber we're
standing in now.
This vehicle appears at every station
simultaneously, giving the illusion
that there are a great number of them,
when actually, it's only the one!
As for where in the universe
this train exists... that's a secret!
Our competitors aren't allowed to
know about things like that.
All you need to know is that
it's a train with infinite entrances
and infinite exits!
That's the power of spacetime magic!

The air in the bathing area is warm and fragrant.
Flower petals decorate the water's surface, and
a light steam embraces the pair as they enter.
They have the whole bath to themselves.
Mochi has already gone on ahead.
She beckons for Treat to join her in the water.
The wolf hesitates, gathering her resolve,
before finally taking a step forward.
She can't act too nervous around her dear friend.
Every action is carefully measured, as to not
make Mochi feel uncomfortable.
...But Mochi has never felt uncomfortable.
Treat knows she's been overly cautious,
but there's just no getting around it.
Being honest about her feelings would change things.
It would definitely change things...
As Treat slips into the comfort of the hot springs,
she thinks...

Maybe something DOES need to change.
But that would mean making a choice.
And she can only choose one.

...Ah, but didn't she decide just now?

Move Picture: 5, Upper Left (0,0), (100%,100%), 100, Normal, @30, Wait

The air suddenly feels thicker.

Mochi is sitting on her lap now...
When did that happen?
Treat couldn't tell if Mochi was able to read
her thoughts, but there were times when it certainly
felt that way.
This was one of those times.
She had wished Mochi would decide for her.
To so kindly offer her hand and suggest they try
becoming more than friends.
For a night, for an hour--anything would do.
To casually suggest, like Moxie did, that they
could mess around a little.

So that Treat would be able to casually accept.

Move Picture: 5, Upper Left (0,0), (100%,100%), 180, Normal, @30, Wait

as if to say,

"It's alright. I know."
And so Treat was able to melt into those kisses.

And get carried away...

The air in the bathing area is warm and fragrant.
Flower petals decorate the water's surface, and
a light steam embraces the group as they enter.
They have the whole bath to themselves.
Moxie, hurrying ahead of her friends, calls out
a challenge to race to the bath. Mochi gives a
gentle reminder of the "no running" rule,
despite breaking into a small jog herself.
Treat's pace remains completely unchanged
as Moxie splashes into the water, with Mochi
not far behind.
She can't help but smile at the scene.
It was times like this that Treat felt the happiest.
Living with Mochi and getting to spend so much
time with her was wonderful.
Of course, she had been close with Moxie, too.
But nothing felt better than when they were
all able to be together.
She wanted that.
Always. More than anything.
As Treat slips into the comfort of the hot springs
with her two, dear friends...

She thinks carefully about how to proceed.

Move Picture: 5, Upper Left (0,0), (100%,100%), 100, Normal, @30, Wait

The air feels thicker now.

Mochi and Moxie look at Treat expectantly.
Kindly... patiently.
She loves Mochi.
And she tells her as much.

To which, she is rewarded with a kiss.
She loves Moxie, too.
And she tells her as well.

To which, she is rewarded with another kiss.
It isn't fair, right?

As a wolf, this kind of thing just isn't an option.
She thought it wasn't an option at all.
Wolves are bad.
And Treat is a bad wolf.
So it isn't fair for her to be able to
feel this much happiness, is it?

Move Picture: 5, Upper Left (0,0), (100%,100%), 180, Normal, @30, Wait

She cries at the thought,
and her partners understand.

They hold her gently.
Ah, how kind.
It's so warm, with each of them on either side.

She briefly worries about overheating in the bath,
but those fears soon melt away.
To be held, and kissed, and touched,
by the both of them like this...

Is far too much for the wolf's lonely heart.
And things get...

REALLY carried away...

When [what is this place?]

The InsteRail uses spacial and
temporal magic in order to transport
matter anywhere in an instant!
It's primarily used for long distance
traversal, but we also offer limited
time travel services to customers
with an Anytime Pass.
Time travel is VERY expensive though.
You'd need to be licensed to use it,
due to regulations against frivolous
creation of alternate universes.
Anyway, we hope you'll get the most
out of our spatial travel services.

When [how does it work?]

The InsteRail is a railway system
with stations all over the world,
even spanning across dimensions!
As long as the rails between stations
are connected, you'll be able to
access them via this chamber we're
standing in now.
This vehicle appears at every station
simultaneously, giving the illusion
that there are a great number of them,
when actually, it's only the one!
As for where in the universe
this train exists... that's a secret!
Our competitors aren't allowed to
know about things like that.
All you need to know is that
it's a train with infinite entrances
and infinite exits!
That's the power of spacetime magic!

When [who are you?]

spatial distortion magic.

her tears were my light?

I hope you'll like it!

page 2

They killed all those wolves.
They killed them and stuffed them.
They were left there in that basement
this whole time.
I-it was... a long time ago, wasn't it?
Things were different back then....
Annie.
Y...yes...?
You can't defend what those rabbits did.
Even if you grew up here.
I'm not defending them!
I-I... I just remember what things were like
when I was a child... the adults always spoke
as if we were at war.
Every winter, the wolves would come closer
to Frosting... so the adults would protect us--
From wolves like Treat?
No, not like Treat...!
There was a big bad wolf--
He was truly dangerous!
How dangerous could he have been?
His head is mounted on a wall.
I... I know for a fact that some of the adults
lost their lives because of the wolves!
I'm not trying to say that they deserved THAT,
I just want to be clear about the facts!
By claiming it was self-defense after all?
Is that what "protection" looks like?
Stop, please...!
Please don't fight...
I don't think we're going to be able to
have a productive conversation about this.
Why don't we all get some rest and
discuss things tomorrow morning?
No, I can't leave it at this!
I'm not suspicious of wolves...!
I've come to care very deeply
for our dear employee, Treat!
ALL of us were afraid of her when she first arrived...
Because of this town's history... because of
the stories we were told when we were younger.
I'm not saying those stories were right.
They were, in fact, very wrong! But...
The taxidermy... that nonsense was left
in the past. We don't do that anymore!
How can you say it's in the past when
a wolf's HEAD is STILL ON DISPLAY?!
Mochi is right.
And with what they did to the garden...
Things are clearly only escalating.
Please stop fighting...
Please....
What I want to say is that no wolves have
come to Frosting in many, many years,
so there hasn't been any violence...
I truly had not considered what things back then
might have been like from the wolves' perspective
until meeting Treat... I'm deeply regretful for this.
Why don't we hear a wolf's perspective, then?
Tell us your opinion of all this, Treat.
....
That's ENOUGH. You're out of line, Mochi...
Treat has been sick with worry
this entire night.
Don't involve her in your argument.
....
Right... that's right.
I'm being mean.
I'm sorry.
It's okay...
I know you're upset.
It's important to remember that we all
care for each other here.
Let's support one another, yes?
I apologize.
Truly.
Yeah... sorry for fighting.
We're all on the same side, aren't we?
Get some rest, you two.
It's been a long night.

"The All-in-one Book of Lore, Book 1"

Show Choices: "Our Origins", "Other Worlds", put it away

When ["Our Origins"]

"The people of this world can be grouped into
three categories: animal folk, witches, and
non-magical humans. While there is some overlap,
our human forms are our single uniting factor.
"Animal folk are born in a wide variety of forms,
believed to be their true forms, which they are
able to return to under various conditions, and
which they MUST return to at death.
"The main identifying factor of a witch is their
ability to command magic of all sorts. Though
they are capable of transforming themselves,
their natural state is humanoid.
"Non-magical humans are classified by their
lack of inherent abilities or talents relating
to magic, as the name suggests. Like witches,
they are born and die in human form.
"The most broadly accepted theory of humankind's
origin is that witches divided into each group:
one set cursed to their strange inhuman forms,
and another set who abandoned magic entirely.
"It is also plausible to say non-magical humans
are the ones who learned magic to become witches,
giving way to an obsession with transformation,
which then led to the existence of animal folk...
"...but until we find evidence favoring either of
these theories, we can only hopelessly guess.
It remains the world's greatest mystery."

When ["Other Worlds"]

"There is no current estimate toward the number
of alternate worlds in existence, though we have
been able to travel to a small handful due to
the efforts of powerful witches.
"The most notable world we have been able to
connect to is known as the Netherworld. This realm
is inhabited by creatures called demons, and
has gone largely unexplored due to its vastness.
"We have very little information on other worlds
and their histories, but it is abundantly clear
something higher than magic has bridged the gaps
between existing worlds long before us.
"Although the worlds we know have all developed
independently, there are striking, impossible to
ignore similarities between them: specifically
the common humanoid forms, and the names of gods.
"The existence of gods is surrounded by mystery.
Most of the information gathered on the subject
is unreliable, as many legends have been passed
down through unverifiable oral tradition.
"Though gods are elusive in nature, the fact that
they are known by the same names across dimensions
is proof enough for many that they truly do exist."

When [put it away]

"The All-in-one Book of Lore, Book 2"

Show Choices: "More on Witches", "History of Animal Folk", put it away

When ["More on Witches"]

"Witches are often deceptive in nature due to
the flexibility their magic allows them.
Transformative spells are incredibly common,
as they take great stock in appearances.
"Non-magical humans are historically distrustful of
witches for their willingness to deceive others.
It is said that a disregard for integrity is the
logical consequence of being able to bend reality.
"Certain breeds of animal folk seem more drawn to
witches than others, even entering into master-
servant type relationships. In those cases, they
are referred to as familiars, or pets.
"Much like the other types of humans, witches
generally prefer the company of their own kind.
This has led to the creation of many witch towns
across the world. Quite a few are magic-exclusive.
"Every witch is born with a predetermined amount of
magic to be used throughout their lifespan, and are
said to be immortal until that magic runs out.*
*This has yet to be proven but is widely supported.
"Magic cannot be transferred except via inheritance
from parent to offspring. If a witch could find a
way around this rule, they could theoretically
use magic transfer to achieve immortality.
"For that potential alone, witches are easily
regarded as the most powerful beings native to
this world."

When ["History of Animal Folk"]

"Humankind's history is riddled with injustice
and oppression, with animal folk often receiving
a disproportionate amount of cruel and unusual
treatment from witches, humans, and each other."
"Within animal folk societies, food chains have
been known to develop in similar patterns.
Certain species are inclined to carnivorous habits,
while others remain herbivores.
"Predators often form tribes to prey on others,
seeking the delicious meat obtained from a
successful hunt. Certain meats are considered
to be irresistible depending on the species.
"The meat of many birds, fish, and mammals are
also popular with witches and non-magical humans.
Meat consumption was previously avoided due to
ethical issues, up until the recent era..."
"...when agriculture alone became unable to
sustain the world's growing population.
Despite humanity's natural aversion
to homicide, desperation won out.
"The witches created an industry out of enchanting
unborn animal folk to never develop their human
forms. This resulted in animal meat becoming
much more socially acceptable to indulge in.
"Since that turning point, food shortages have been
exceedingly rare. Through the sacrifice of select
species of animal folk, we have all been able to
continue to thrive in this world."

see you again.

steal anything!

I'm not a snitch...
That's a relief...!
You're a witch, not a snitch!
Why are you here anyway?
I was curious...
Since the protest, I started to wonder
if it's really okay to eat chickens.

if we're all made of the same meat,
then the people here at this factory
are committing mass murder.

that wolves like you don't kill to eat...

wrongfully persecuted.
My friends would be happy
to hear you say all that!
You'd make a good activist!

to learn more about chickens and the
meat production process, but they
wouldn't give me a tour...
Why not?
They don't hire high school students...
the lady told me to ask my teacher
to arrange a field trip instead.
Oh... well...
It's nice that you tried!
Good luck... on your rescue mission.
Thanks!

Show Choices: what is this place?, how does it work?, who are you?, nevermind

When [what is this place?]

The InsteRail uses spacial and
temporal magic in order to transport
matter anywhere in an instant!
It's primarily used for long distance
traversal, but we also offer limited
time travel services to customers
with an Anytime Pass.
Time travel is VERY expensive though.
You'd need to be licensed to use it,
due to regulations against frivolous
creation of alternate universes.
Anyway, we hope you'll get the most
out of our spatial travel services.

When [how does it work?]

The InsteRail is a railway system
with stations all over the world,
even spanning across dimensions!
As long as the rails between stations
are connected, you'll be able to
access them via this chamber we're
standing in now.
This vehicle appears at every station
simultaneously, giving the illusion
that there are a great number of them,
when actually, it's only the one!
As for where in the universe
this train exists... that's a secret!
Our competitors aren't allowed to
know about things like that.
All you need to know is that
it's a train with infinite entrances
and infinite exits!
That's the power of spacetime magic!

When [who are you?]

You can call me Spice!
I'm a witch who specializes in
spatial distortion magic.
My doll's name is Nil!

knowing none of that was real.

The greatest tragedy of them all...
that the consequences my magnificent tale
will cease to exist once we fade to black!
No matter the tragedy, I will always protect
the sanctity of the TRUE ENDING.
There's no need to fall into despair.
But if you WOULD like to fall,
remember that I, Lilium, will
always be here waiting for you~!
Until we meet again.

he seems to have adopted a pet!

Grenadine,
Your last reply was terse as always.

just pleasantries--I AM truly curious!
I realized the anniversary of the worst day
of our lives has passed us by once again.
Fifteen years! I can hardly believe it.
I'm actually writing you to give my new address.
I'm running the Naturalist Reserve in Hosta Swamp.
You're welcome to come and visit!

How are things in Agaricus?

I have fabulous news.

one of the frog girls here as my own.
Following in Myrrh's footsteps, I suppose!
Maybe it's about time you adopt a child
of your own, eh? It'd make us three for three!

Yours truly,
Capillaire

Myrrh... your master.

Play BGM: 'grenadine', 100, 100

Fadein Screen

He was overly idealistic...
the revolutionary type.
Thought he could change
the world for the better.
I was... enchanted by his words,
at the time. The naivety of youth.
And so, Myrrh, Capillaire, and I...
The three of us came together
to write a certain book.
Our goal was to explain the mechanics
of this world as we understood them.
Pointing out injustice. Illuminating the
oppressive systems we're all trapped in.
That book was met with its fair share
of criticism. We got things wrong.
We learned more... heard from other activists.
Two humans and a witch... we hadn't
consulted any animal folk when writing
that first volume. Foolishly, we spread
the very misinformation we tried to combat.
But the second book... ohh, the reaction
was far worse. We'd developed a reputation
by then, as controversial authors.
The critics tore our writing to shreds.
Myrrh and I faced the worst of the harassment.
He was so ashamed... the books were his idea
in the first place. He took it very personally.
That coward... he left me behind
to deal with the aftermath on my own.
I did my best to clean up his mess.
Meanwhile, Capillaire... he just carried on
his merry way. Didn't seem to care at all
that our names were completely tarnished!
But he's always been that way...
I envied him for a long time.
In the end, I abandoned my dream of
ever becoming a celebrated author.
After many years of practicing alchemy...
I ended up here, with my own clinic.
And that's all there is to it.

Fadeout Screen

...It's been a long, long time since
I've spoken about any of that.
Thank you for listening.
